questions.question: The number of deaths during the first 28 completed days of life per 1000 live births in a given year or period is defined as ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**neonatal mortality rate**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The number of deaths during the first 28 completed days of life per 1000 live births** in a given year or period is defined as **the neonatal mortality rate**.
 
• There are some concerns about the quality of neonatal mortality reporting both internationally and within states, particularly in terms of defining a live birth and/or reporting both birth and death certificates for newborns with very low birth weights.
 
• When neonatal death certificates are matched to corresponding birth certificates, much more additional and valuable data (birth weight, mother's smoking status, when prenatal care began, etc.) is obtained for neonatal mortality risk analysis.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The number of newborn deaths per 1,000 live births is known as t**he infant mortality rate. **
 
• **The infant mortality rate** is an essential indicator of a society's general health, in addition to providing crucial information regarding maternal and baby health.
 
• **The crude mortality rate **is derived by dividing the number of fatalities in a particular time by the number of people who were at risk of dying during that period.
 
• A death rate that is limited to a certain age group is known as an **age-specific mortality rate.**

questions.question: The Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act 2009 is an Act of Parliament which came into force in:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2010**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act 2009** is an Act of Parliament that came into force in **2010**.
 
• **On August 4, 2009, the Indian Parliament** passed the Right to Education Act 2009, popularly known as the RTE Act 2009.
 
• It explains the importance of free and compulsory education for children aged 6 to 14 years in India, as defined by Article 21 (A) of the Indian Constitution.
 
• **On April 1, 2010, **this act took effect, making India one of **135 countries **to make education a fundamental right for all children.
 
• It establishes basic standards for elementary schools, forbids unrecognized schools from operating, and opposes donation fees and kid admission interviews.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• Through frequent surveys, the Right to Education Act keeps tabs on all neighbourhoods and identifies children who are eligible for but lack the financial means to receive an education.
 
• For many years, India has had educational difficulties at** both the national and state levels.**
 
• **The Right to Education Act of 2009** establishes roles and obligations for the national government, states, and local governments in order to close gaps in their educational systems and improve the country's educational quality.

questions.question:
Which of the following statements is/are correct regarding the mountains?

I- Mountains may be arranged in a line known as range.

II- The Aravali range in India is one of the oldest fold mountain systems in the world.

III- Mt. Kilimanjaro in South America is an example of a Volcanic Mountain.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Only I and II**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Mountains** are sometimes organised in a **line called a range**. Many mountain ranges are made up of a series of** parallel ranges** that stretch for hundreds of kilometres sometimes such a line known as a mountain range. ***Hence statement 1 is correct.***
 
• **The Himalayas, Alps, and the Andes are Asian, European, and South American mountain** ranges, respectively.
 
• **The Aravallis **in Northwestern India are one of the world's oldest fold mountains, forming remnant mountains with elevations ranging from** 300 to 900 metres. *Hence statement 2 is correct.***
 
• They reach 800 kilometres from Gujarat's Himmatnagar to Delhi's 692 kilometres, encompassing **Haryana, Rajasthan, Gujarat, and Delhi.** 
 
• **At 5,895 metres, Mount Kilimanjaro** is Africa's tallest mountain (19,340 feet).
 
• It is the world's tallest free-standing mountain rise, meaning it exists independently of any mountain range.
 
• **Kilimanjaro**, also known as a stratovolcano (a big volcano comprised of ash, lava, and rock), is made up of three cones: **Kibo, Mawenzi, **and **Shira.**
 
• Mt. Kilimanjaro is a volcanic mountain but it lies in Africa, not in South America.. ***Hence statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
• The mountain's top and the tallest of the three volcanic structures is **Kibo**.

questions.question: The idea of having a provision for a Bicameral Parliament in the Constitution of India was borrowed from the ______ Constitution.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**British**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The idea of having a provision for a Bicameral Parliament** in the Constitution of India was borrowed from the** British Constitution**. 
 
• **The Government of India Act of 1919, **commonly known as the Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms, took effect in 1921.
 
• It was the first time in the country that** bicameralism** and direct elections were implemented.
 
• The Indian Legislative Council was therefore replaced with a bicameral legislature with an Upper House (Council of State) and a Lower House (Legislative Assembly).
 
• Direct election was used to elect the majority of members of both Houses.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 Canada
 
 
 
 
• Federation with a strong Centre
 
• Vesting of residuary powers in the Centre

questions.question: A ______ tank is an underground chamber made of concrete, fiberglass, or plastic through which domestic wastewater (sewage) flows for basic treatment.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**septic**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **A septic tank** is concrete, fibreglass, or plastic subterranean chamber through which domestic wastewater (sewage) flows for basic treatment.
 
• Anaerobic action occurs within the septic tank. The term "septic" refers to the anaerobic bacterial environment that forms in the tank and decomposes the waste that is expelled.
 
• **Domestic sewage**, as well as animal and poultry wastes, are examples of N-rich materials that supply nutrients for anaerobic organism development and multiplication.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• A pressure/vacuum vent is installed in** pressure tanks** to avoid venting loss due to boiling and breathing loss due to daily temperature or barometric pressure variations.

questions.question:
Which of the following is an example of monosaccharides?

A. Fructose B. Sucrose C. Starch D. Glucose
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both A and D**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Hexoses, glucose, and fructose **are the most common **monosaccharides found in fruits and vegetables.**
 
• **Fructose** is a monosaccharide, a form of sugar. Fructose, like other sugars, has four calories per gram.
 
• Fructose is often known as **"fruit sugar" **since it is found in many fruits naturally. Other plant foods that include it include honey, sugar beets, sugar cane, and vegetables.
 
• The main sugar in human blood is** glucose**. It is the human body's major source of energy and comes from the food you eat.
 
• Human blood transports glucose to all of the human body's cells for energy production. Diabetes is a condition in which blood sugar levels are abnormally high.​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Monosaccharides**, often known as simple sugars, are the most basic sugar molecules (monomers) from which all carbohydrates are constructed.
 
• They are usually white, crystalline solids that are water-soluble. Only a few monosaccharides have a sweet flavour, despite their name (sugars).
 
• Disaccharides (such as sucrose and lactose) and polysaccharides are made up of monosaccharides (such as cellulose and starch).
 
• The common table sugar, sucrose, is a disaccharide that contains one molecule of each of the two monosaccharides D-glucose and D-fructose.

• **President Bidya Devi Bhandari **bestowed the honorary rank of General of the Nepali Army to Indian Army Chief General M. M. Naravane during a special event, continuing a decades-old practice that highlights the strong links between the two militaries.

questions.question: Poor sanitation conditions may NOT be the likely reason behind which of the following diseases/conditions?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Arthritis**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Poor sanitation conditions** may NOT be the likely reason behind **Arthritis**.
 
• **Arthritis **is a condition in which one or more joints enlarge and become tender. Joint pain and stiffness are the most common symptoms of arthritis, which normally worsen with age.
 
• Osteoarthritis and rheumatoid arthritis are the two most frequent kinds of arthritis. Cartilage — the firm, slippery tissue that covers the ends of bones where they form a joint — breaks down as a result of osteoarthritis.
 
• **Rheumatoid arthritis** is an autoimmune illness in which the immune system destroys the joints, starting with the lining.
 
• Diarrhoeal disorders including cholera and dysentery, as well as typhoid, intestinal worm infections, and polio, are all connected to** poor sanitation**. Stunting is exacerbated by poor nutrition, which also leads to the spread of antibiotic resistance.
 
• Children are in danger of childhood infections and malnutrition as a result of poor sanitation, which can have a negative influence on their general development, learning, and, later in life, economic opportunities.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The poliovirus causes polio**, a debilitating and potentially fatal disease. The virus can infect a person's spinal cord, causing paralysis (the inability to move parts of the body).
 
• **Typhoid fever** is a bacterial infection that can infect multiple organs and spread throughout the body.
 
• **Cholera** is a bacterial infection that is spread by drinking contaminated water.

questions.question: Which two kings fought in the Battle of Hydaspes?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Alexander and Porus**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **In 326 BC, Alexander the Great** faced **King Porus in the Battle of the Hydaspes**, also known as the **Battle of Jhelum**.
 
• It took place on the banks of the** Jhelum River** (called as Hydaspes by the ancient Greeks) in the **Punjab area **of India (modern-day Punjab, Pakistan).
 
• The conflict ended with a Greek triumph and Porus' capitulation.
 
• Large swaths of Punjab were integrated into the Alexandrian Empire, and Alexander reinstalled the vanquished and dethroned Porus as a subordinate ruler.
 
• One of Alexander's "masterpieces" was his choice to cross the monsoon-swollen river despite intense Indian monitoring in order to catch Porus' army off-guard.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Alexander III of Macedon**, also known as** Alexander the Great,** was the monarch of Macedon in ancient Greece.
 
• At the age of 20, he succeeded his father Philip II to the throne in 336 BC and spent the majority of his reign executing a lengthy military campaign across Western Asia and Northeastern Africa.
 
• He had built one of the biggest empires in history by the age of thirty, ranging from Greece to northwestern India.
 
• **Porus** was an ancient Indian king whose kingdom stretched between the Hydaspes (Jhelum River) and the Acesines (Chenab River) in the Punjab area of India.

questions.question: ______ refers to a sanitation system in which toilets collect human excreta in sealable, removable cartridges that are transported to treatment facilities.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Container-Based sanitation**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Container-based sanitation (CBS) **is a sanitation method in which toilets collect human waste and transport it to treatment facilities in **sealable, removable containers **(also known as cartridges).
 
• This method of sanitation entails the use of a commercial service that offers specific types of portable toilets and distributes empty containers when full ones are picked up. The service carries excreta and carefully disposes of or reuses it.
 
• The users are normally responsible for the cost of excreta collection. CBS can be utilised to offer low-income urban areas safe collection, transportation, and treatment of faeces at a lesser cost than establishing and maintaining sewers with the right development, support, and collaborations.
 
• **Sanitation systems **based on containers are a low-cost option. They can be employed in quickly increasing cities, refugee camps, and disaster relief circumstances.
 
• They are in line with Sustainable Development Goal 6 of the United Nations, which is to "provide sanitation for all by 2030."

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Ecological sanitation** is a method of sanitation that tries to safely reuse human waste in agriculture.
 
• It is a concept, not a technology or a device, that is defined by a goal to "complete the loop" between sanitation and agriculture in a safe manner, primarily for nutrients and organic matter.
 
• The disposal of human waste without the use of water as a carrier is known as **dry sanitation.**
 
• **CLTS (Community Led Total Sanitation)** is an innovative approach to mobilizing communities to prevent open defecation (OD). Communities are given the tools they need to assess and analyze open defecation (OD) and take steps to achieve ODF (open defecation free).

questions.question: The pilgrimage sites of Nashik, Triyambak and Bhadrachalam lie on the banks of which of the following rivers?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Godavari**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Trimbakeshwar Jyotirlinga Temple** is situated on the **Godavari River's banks.**
 
• **Maharashtra's Nashik **district is home to the temple.
 
• In Andhra Pradesh's Krishna district, the Krishna River flows from Mahabaleshwar to the Bay of Bengal.
 
• **The Sri Sita Ramachandra Swamy temple** is a Hindu shrine dedicated to Rama, the god Vishnu's most famous avatar.
 
• It lies in the town of Bhadrachalam, Telangana, India, on the banks of the Godavari River.
 
• It's one among the country's 12 Jyotirlingas. After the Ganga, the Godavari is the longest river.
 
• Its source is in **Trimbakeshwar, Nashik, Maharashtra. **
 
• The rivers Narmada, Johila, and Son all emerge near Amarkantak in Madhya Pradesh.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **The Krishna River** is a river on India's Deccan plateau that is the country's third-longest river after the Ganges and Godavari, and the fourth-largest in terms of water inputs and basin area after the Ganges, Indus, and the Godavari.
 
• **The Brahmaputra** is a transboundary river that flows through Tibet, China, India, and Bangladesh. It is also known as the Yarlung Tsangpo in Tibet, the Siang/Dihang River in Arunachal Pradesh, and Luit in Assamese.
 
• **The Narmada River, **also known as the Reva and originally as Narbada or anglicized as Nerbudda, is India's 5th longest river and overall biggest west-flowing river.

questions.question: Which bank is referred to as ‘The lender of last resort’?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Central Bank**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The central bank **is referred to as **‘The lender of last resort'.**
 
• **A lender of last resort (LoR)** is a financial institution, usually, a country's central bank, that provides loans to banks and other qualifying entities that are in financial distress or are regarded as highly hazardous or on the verge of collapse.
 
• The lender of last resort serves to protect depositors and to prevent panicked clients from withdrawing funds from banks with temporary low liquidity.
 
• Commercial banks often avoid borrowing from lenders of last resort since doing so shows that the bank is in financial distress.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **A central bank** is a financial entity that administers a country's commercial banking system and regulates its currency and monetary policy. A central bank, unlike a commercial bank, has a monopoly on growing the monetary base.
 
• **The State Bank of India **is a multinational public sector bank and statutory organisation located in Mumbai, Maharashtra, India. SBI is the 43rd largest bank in the world, and it is the only Indian bank in the Fortune Global 500 list of the world's largest enterprises for 2020.
 
• **Dena Bank **was a state-owned bank that merged with Bank of Baroda in 2019.

questions.question: Why is water fluoridation, which is the controlled adjustment of fluoride to public water supply, done?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**To prevent tooth decay**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Water fluoridation **is the addition of fluoride to a public water supply with** the express purpose of preventing tooth deca**y.
 
• **Fluoridated water **contains a sufficient amount of fluoride to prevent cavities; this can occur naturally or through the addition of fluoride.
 
• Fluoridated water works on dental surfaces by producing low levels of fluoride in saliva, which slows the demineralization of tooth enamel and speeds up the remineralization of tooth enamel in the early stages of cavities.
 
• In most industrialised countries, tooth decay is still a serious public health concern, impacting** 60–90 percent of kids and the vast majority of adults**.
 
• Fluoridation of drinking water decreases cavities in children, but its effectiveness in adults is unclear.​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Damage to a tooth's surface,** or enamel, is known as **tooth decay.**
 
• It occurs when oral bacteria produce acids that destroy the enamel.
 
• Cavities (dental caries) are holes in your teeth caused by tooth decay.
 
• If left untreated, dental decay can lead to discomfort, infection, and even tooth loss.

questions.question: As per the Economic Survey 2020–21, net FPI (Foreign Portfolio Investment) recorded an all-time monthly high of US$9.8 billion in ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**November 2020**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• With global asset shifts towards equities and prospects of a faster recovery in emerging economies, India remained a preferred foreign investment destination in FY21, with Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) pouring in.
 
• As risk appetite began to recover, net FPI (Foreign Portfolio Investments) inflows reached an all-time monthly high of US$9.8 billion in November 2020.
 
• Furthermore, in 2020, India was the only major economy to attract equity Foreign Institutional Investments (FII).
 
• The economy's liquidity condition is solid, and the stock market has reached previously inconceivable heights in recent months.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• Securities and other financial assets held by investors in another nation are referred to as** foreign portfolio investments (FPI).**
 
• It does not provide the investor's actual ownership of a company's assets and, depending on market volatility, is relatively liquid.

questions.question: Under which of the following rulers did Delhi first become a capital?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Tomara Rajputs**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Tomara Rajputs,** who were vanquished by the Chauhans (also known as Chahamanas) of **Ajmer in the middle of the twelfth century, **established Delhi as the capital of a kingdom.
 
• **Delhi **grew in importance as a commercial centre during** the Tomaras and Chauhans.**
 
• The city was home to many wealthy Jaina merchants who built multiple temples.
 
• The Dehliwal coins, which were made here, were widely circulated.
 
• The creation of the Delhi Sultanate in the early thirteenth century began the transition of Delhi into a city that governed broad swaths of the subcontinent.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **The Chauhans** were the feudatories of the Gurjar-Pratiharas, who helped Nagabhatta I defeat and safeguard the boundaries from Arab invasions during the Battle of Rajasthan.
 
• **Ajayaraj Chauhan, the Chauhan king of Sakambhari,** founded the city of Ajayameru, which later became known as Ajmer.
 
• **The Slave dynasty's** third and greatest Delhi sultan was Iltutmish. Iltutmish was sold into slavery, but he married the daughter of his master, Qutub ud-din Aibak, in 1211.
 
• **Between 1290 to 1320, the Khilji dynasty **governed the Delhi Sultanate, which included significant swaths of the Indian subcontinent.

questions.question: The efforts of Siddhendra Yogi have brought glory to the dance form called ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kuchipudi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Kuchipudi** is one of India's eight primary classical dance forms. It comes from Kuchipudi, a village in the Indian state of** Andhra Pradesh.**
 
• It is a dance-drama genre that originated in the ancient Hindu Sanskrit scripture Natya Shastra.
 
• Like all of India's great classical dances, it began as a religious art form tied to itinerant bards, temples, and spiritual beliefs.
 
• Copper inscriptions from the 10th century and books like the Machupalli Kaifat from the 15th century show that Kuchipudi existed in an earlier iteration.
 
• According to Kuchipudi legend, in the 17th century, Tirtha Narayana Yati, an Advaita Vedanta Sanyasin, and his disciple, an orphan named** Siddhendra Yogi,** developed and systematised the present style of Kuchipudi.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Mohiniyattam **is an Indian traditional dance genre that originated in Kerala and has remained popular ever since. Mohiniyattam dance takes its name from Mohini, a historical enchantress avatar of the Hindu God Vishnu who uses her feminine skills to assist good triumph over evil.
 
• **Kathakali** is a popular genre of Indian classical dance. It's a "story play" kind of art, but it's differentiated by the traditionally male actor-dancer's lavishly colourful make-up, costumes, and face masks.
 
• **Bharatanatyam** is a significant Hindu form of Indian classical dance. The initial origins of Bharatanatyam are regarded to be Bharata Muni's Natya Shastra and Nandikeshvara's Abhinaya Darpana.

questions.question: In which of the following Indian states will you find the Buxa Fort?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**West Bengal**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Buxa Fort **is located in the Buxa Tiger Reserve, in the **Kalchini CD block of the Alipurduar subdivision **of the Alipurduar district, **West Bengal,** at an elevation of 867 metres (2,844 feet).
 
• **Alipurduar, **the nearest town, is 30 kilometres (19 miles) away.
 
• The fort was utilised by the Bhutanese King to secure the section of the border between Tibet and India that passed through Bhutan.
 
• Hundreds of refugees arrived at the location afterwards, during the upheaval in Tibet's occupation, and used the abandoned fort as a haven.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Buxa Tiger Reserve **is a tiger reserve and national park in northern West Bengal, India, that spans 760 square kilometres.
 
• It varies in altitude from 60 metres in the Gangetic Plains to 1,750 metres on the Himalayan border in the north.
 
• The reserve is home to at least 284 different bird species.
